sanskrit: sātyakir uvāca dhanaṃjayasya padavīṃ dharmarājasya śāsanāt gacchāmi svasti te brahman na me kālātyayo bhavet
english: Sātyaki said: At the command of the Dharma-king I am following the track of Dhanaṃjaya. Fare you well, O brāhmaṇa—let no time of mine be lost.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etāvad uktvā śaineya ācāryaṃ parivarjayan prayātaḥ sahasā rājan sārathiṃ cedam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Having said only this much, O king, the grandson of Śini avoided the preceptor and swiftly drove on, and he spoke thus to his charioteer:

sanskrit: droṇaḥ kariṣyate yatnaṃ sarvathā mama vāraṇe yatto yāhi raṇe sūta śṛṇu cedaṃ vacaḥ param
english: Droṇa will make every effort to bar my way. Drive on with care in the battle, O charioteer, and hear besides this further word of mine.

sanskrit: etad ālokyate sainyam āvantyānāṃ mahāprabham asyānantaratas tv etad dākṣiṇātyaṃ mahābalam
english: There is seen the army of the Āvantyas, of great splendour; and next to it that mighty host of the southerners.

sanskrit: tadanantaram etac ca bāhlikānāṃ balaṃ mahat bāhlikābhyāśato yuktaṃ karṇasyāpi mahad balam
english: And next to that is this great force of the Bāhlikas; and close beside the Bāhlikas, joined with them, is also the mighty host of Karṇa.

sanskrit: anyonyena hi sainyāni bhinnāny etāni sārathe anyonyaṃ samupāśritya na tyakṣyanti raṇājiram
english: These armies, though distinct one from another, O charioteer, lean each upon the other and will not abandon the field of battle.

sanskrit: etad antaram āsādya codayāśvān prahṛṣṭavat madhyamaṃ javam āsthāya vaha mām atra sārathe
english: Reaching the gap between them, urge on the horses gladly; holding a middling pace, carry me through there, O charioteer.

sanskrit: bāhlikā yatra dṛśyante nānāpraharaṇodyatāḥ dākṣiṇātyāś ca bahavaḥ sūtaputrapurogamāḥ
english: There where the Bāhlikas are seen, raising their varied weapons, and the many southerners with the Sūta's son at their head—

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathasaṃbādhaṃ yac cānīkaṃ vilokyate nānādeśasamutthaiś ca padātibhir adhiṣṭhitam
english: and that division which is seen thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots, and beset with foot-soldiers risen from many lands—

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā yantāraṃ brahmāṇaṃ parivarjayan sa vyatīyāya yatrograṃ karṇasya sumahad balam
english: Having said this much to his driver, and shunning the brāhmaṇa, he passed on to where stood the fierce and exceeding mighty force of Karṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇo 'nuyayau kruddho vikiran viśikhān bahūn yuyudhānaṃ mahābāhuṃ gacchantam anivartinam
english: Wrathful, Droṇa pursued him, scattering many shafts—Yuyudhāna the mighty-armed, who advanced and would not turn back.

sanskrit: karṇasya sainyaṃ sumahad abhihatya śitaiḥ śaraiḥ prāviśad bhāratīṃ senām aparyantāṃ sa sātyakiḥ
english: Having struck Karṇa's great host with his sharp arrows, that Sātyaki entered the boundless Bhārata army.

sanskrit: praviṣṭe yuyudhāne tu sainikeṣu druteṣu ca amarṣī kṛtavarmā tu sātyakiṃ paryavārayat
english: When Yuyudhāna had entered and the soldiers had fled, the unforbearing Kṛtavarman moved to hem Sātyaki in on every side.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ viśikhaiḥ ṣaḍbhir āhatya sātyakiḥ caturbhiś caturo 'syāśvān ājaghānāśu vīryavān
english: As he rushed upon him, the valiant Sātyaki struck him with six shafts and swiftly smote his four horses with four arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ punaḥ ṣoḍaśabhir nataparvabhir āśugaiḥ sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmāṇaṃ pratyavidhyat stanāntare
english: Then again, with sixteen swift, smooth-jointed arrows, Sātyaki pierced Kṛtavarman in the centre of the chest.

sanskrit: sa tudyamāno viśikhair bahubhis tigmatejanaiḥ sātvatena mahārāja kṛtavarmā na cakṣame
english: Tormented by the Sātvata with many shafts of keen point, O great king, Kṛtavarman could not endure it.

sanskrit: sa vatsadantaṃ saṃdhāya jihmagānalasaṃnibham ākṛṣya rājann ākarṇād vivyādhorasi sātyakim
english: Fitting a calf-tooth arrow, like a fire that flies aslant, and drawing it back to his ear, O king, he pierced Sātyaki in the breast.

sanskrit: sa tasya dehāvaraṇaṃ bhittvā dehaṃ ca sāyakaḥ sapatrapuṅkhaḥ pṛthivīṃ viveśa rudhirokṣitaḥ
english: That arrow, feathered to its butt, having cleft the armour that guarded his body and his body too, entered the earth, drenched with blood.

sanskrit: athāsya bahubhir bāṇair acchinat paramāstravit samārgaṇaguṇaṃ rājan kṛtavarmā śarāsanam
english: Then Kṛtavarman, master of the highest weapons, with many arrows cut asunder Sātyaki's bow, O king, together with its arrow and its string.

sanskrit: vivyādha ca raṇe rājan sātyakiṃ satyavikramam daśabhir viśikhais tīkṣṇair abhikruddhaḥ stanāntare
english: And in fury, O king, he pierced Sātyaki of true valour in the centre of the chest with ten keen shafts in that battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ praśīrṇe dhanuṣi śaktyā śaktimatāṃ varaḥ abhyahan dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: Then, his bow being shattered, Sātyaki, foremost of the mighty, struck Kṛtavarman's right arm with a spear.

sanskrit: tato 'nyat sudṛḍhaṃ vīro dhanur ādāya sātyakiḥ vyasṛjad viśikhāṃs tūrṇaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then the hero Sātyaki, taking up another very stout bow, quickly loosed his shafts by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: sarathaṃ kṛtavarmāṇaṃ samantāt paryavākirat chādayitvā raṇe 'tyarthaṃ hārdikyaṃ tu sa sātyakiḥ
english: That Sātyaki covered Kṛtavarman together with his chariot on every side, and screened the son of Hṛdika utterly in the battle.

sanskrit: athāsya bhallena śiraḥ sāratheḥ samakṛntata sa papāta hataḥ sūto hārdikyasya mahārathāt tatas te yantari hate prādravaṃs turagā bhṛśam
english: Then with a broad-headed shaft he severed the head of his charioteer; slain, the driver of the son of Hṛdika fell from that great car, and, the driver being slain, the horses bolted wildly.

sanskrit: atha bhojas tv asaṃbhrānto nigṛhya turagān svayam tasthau śaradhanuṣpāṇis tat sainyāny abhyapūjayan
english: But the Bhoja chief, unflustered, himself reined in the horses and stood, arrows and bow in hand—and the armies honoured him for it.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam ivāśvasya sadaśvān samacodayat vyapetabhīr amitrāṇām āvahat sumahad bhayam sātyakiś cābhyagāt tasmāt sa tu bhīmam upādravat
english: Having recovered breath for a moment, he urged on his good horses; free of fear, he carried great terror into the foes. Sātyaki passed on from him, while Kṛtavarman rushed upon Bhīma.

sanskrit: yuyudhāno 'pi rājendra droṇānīkād viniḥsṛtaḥ prayayau tvaritas tūrṇaṃ kāmbojānāṃ mahācamūm
english: Yuyudhāna too, O lord of kings, having issued forth from Droṇa's division, sped swiftly and at once toward the great host of the Kāmbojas.

sanskrit: sa tatra bahubhiḥ śūraiḥ saṃniruddho mahārathaiḥ na cacāla tadā rājan sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: Though there hemmed in by many heroic great car-warriors, Sātyaki of true valour did not waver then, O king.

sanskrit: saṃdhāya ca camūṃ droṇo bhoje bhāraṃ niveśya ca anvadhāvad raṇe yatto yuyudhānaṃ yuyutsayā
english: And Droṇa, having marshalled his division and laid the burden of it upon the Bhoja, pursued Yuyudhāna in battle with intent to fight, full of care.

sanskrit: tathā tam anudhāvantaṃ yuyudhānasya pṛṣṭhataḥ nyavārayanta saṃkruddhāḥ pāṇḍusainye bṛhattamāḥ
english: As he thus pursued, following at Yuyudhāna's back, the mightiest warriors in the Pāṇḍava army, greatly enraged, held him off.

sanskrit: samāsādya tu hārdikyaṃ rathānāṃ pravaraṃ ratham pāñcālā vigatotsāhā bhīmasenapurogamāḥ vikramya vāritā rājan vīreṇa kṛtavarmaṇā
english: But the Pāñcālas, with Bhīmasena at their head, having closed with the son of Hṛdika—foremost car among cars—lost their ardour; for though they showed their prowess, they were held back, O king, by the hero Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: yatamānāṃs tu tān sarvān īṣad vigatacetasaḥ abhitas tāñ śaraugheṇa klāntavāhān avārayat
english: All of them, striving on yet somewhat bereft of their senses, their mounts grown weary, he warded off on every side with floods of arrows.

sanskrit: nigṛhītās tu bhojena bhojānīkepsavo raṇe atiṣṭhann āryavad vīrāḥ prārthayanto mahad yaśaḥ
english: Checked by the Bhoja, those heroes who longed to break through the Bhoja division stood their ground in battle like noblemen, seeking great renown.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ sainyam evaṃ pravicitaṃ varam vyūḍham evaṃ yathānyāyam evaṃ bahu ca saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: An army so manifold, so excellently arrayed, so marshalled in due order, and so vast, O Saṃjaya—

sanskrit: nityaṃ pūjitam asmābhir abhikāmaṃ ca naḥ sadā prauḍham atyadbhutākāraṃ purastād dṛḍhavikramam
english: ever honoured by us and ever well-disposed toward us, mature, of most wondrous aspect, and steadfast in valour in the van—

sanskrit: nātivṛddham abālaṃ ca na kṛśaṃ nātipīvaram laghuvṛttāyataprāṇaṃ sāragātram anāmayam
english: neither too old nor too young, neither lean nor over-stout, nimble and long of wind, sturdy of limb and free of sickness—

sanskrit: āttasaṃnāhasaṃpannaṃ bahuśastraparicchadam śastragrahaṇavidyāsu bahvīṣu pariniṣṭhitam
english: furnished with donned armour, equipped with manifold weapons, and perfected in the many arts of wielding arms—

sanskrit: ārohe paryavaskande saraṇe sāntaraplute samyakpraharaṇe yāne vyapayāne ca kovidam
english: skilled in mounting and in leaping down, in charging and in vaulting across, in striking truly, in advancing and in withdrawing—

sanskrit: nāgeṣv aśveṣu bahuśo ratheṣu ca parīkṣitam parīkṣya ca yathānyāyaṃ vetanenopapāditam
english: tested again and again upon elephants, horses, and chariots, and, once duly tested, provided with its wages—

sanskrit: na goṣṭhyā nopacāreṇa na saṃbandhanimittataḥ nānāhūto na hy abhṛto mama sainye babhūva ha
english: in my army there was none who came uninvited, none unpaid—not through mere fellowship, nor flattery, nor by reason of kinship.

sanskrit: kulīnāryajanopetaṃ tuṣṭapuṣṭam anuddhatam kṛtamānopakāraṃ ca yaśasvi ca manasvi ca
english: manned by high-born and honourable folk, contented and well-nourished, unarrogant, shown honour and good service, glorious and high of spirit—

sanskrit: sacivaiś cāparair mukhyair bahubhir mukhyakarmabhiḥ lokapālopamais tāta pālitaṃ narasattamaiḥ
english: and guarded, my son, by other chief counsellors—many of them, doers of foremost deeds, like the guardians of the worlds, those best of men—

sanskrit: bahubhiḥ pārthivair guptam asmatpriyacikīrṣubhiḥ asmān abhisṛtaiḥ kāmāt sabalaiḥ sapadānugaiḥ
english: protected by many kings who sought to do us pleasure, who had come to us of their own desire with their forces and their followers—

sanskrit: mahodadhim ivāpūrṇam āpagābhiḥ samantataḥ apakṣaiḥ pakṣisaṃkāśai rathair aśvaiś ca saṃvṛtam
english: full like the great ocean filled on every side by rivers, encompassed by chariots and horses that, though wingless, were like winged birds—

sanskrit: yodhākṣayyajalaṃ bhīmaṃ vāhanormitaraṅgiṇam kṣepaṇyasigadāśaktiśaraprāsajhaṣākulam
english: a fearsome sea whose inexhaustible waters were its warriors, whose surging waves were its mounts, teeming as with fishes with slings, swords, maces, lances, arrows, and javelins—

sanskrit: dhvajabhūṣaṇasaṃbādhaṃ ratnapaṭṭena saṃcitam vāhanair api dhāvadbhir vāyuvegavikampitam
english: thronged with banners and ornaments, heaped with bands of jewels, and stirred to trembling, as by the speed of the wind, by its onrushing mounts—

sanskrit: droṇagambhīrapātālaṃ kṛtavarmamahāhradam jalasaṃdhamahāgrāhaṃ karṇacandrodayoddhatam
english: with Droṇa for its deep abyss, Kṛtavarman for its great whirlpool, Jalasaṃdha for its mighty shark, and roused high by Karṇa as by the moon's rising—

sanskrit: gate sainyārṇavaṃ bhittvā tarasā pāṇḍavarṣabhe saṃjayaikarathenaiva yuyudhāne ca māmakam
english: when the bull of the Pāṇḍavas had gone, cleaving through that ocean of my host by his swiftness, O Saṃjaya, and Yuyudhāna too, with but a single chariot—

sanskrit: tatra śeṣaṃ na paśyāmi praviṣṭe savyasācini sātvate ca rathodāre mama sainyasya saṃjaya
english: once Savyasācin had entered, and the high-souled Sātvata car-warrior, I see no remnant of my army there, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: tau tatra samatikrāntau dṛṣṭvābhītau tarasvinau sindhurājaṃ ca saṃprekṣya gāṇḍīvasyeṣugocare
english: Seeing those two impetuous and fearless warriors break clean through, and beholding the king of the Sindhus within the range of Gāṇḍīva's arrows—

sanskrit: kiṃ tadā kuravaḥ kṛtyaṃ vidadhuḥ kālacoditāḥ dāruṇaikāyane kāle kathaṃ vā pratipedire
english: what task did the Kurus then set themselves, driven on by fate? And how did they bear themselves in that dread and narrow pass of time?

sanskrit: grastān hi kauravān manye mṛtyunā tāta saṃgatān vikramo hi raṇe teṣāṃ na tathā dṛśyate 'dya vai
english: For I think the Kauravas are seized, my son, gripped close by death; for their prowess in battle no longer shows itself today as it once did.

sanskrit: akṣatau saṃyuge tatra praviṣṭau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau na ca vārayitā kaś cit tayor astīha saṃjaya
english: Unhurt, Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava have penetrated into that battle, and there is no one here to bar them, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: bhṛtāś ca bahavo yodhāḥ parīkṣyaiva mahārathāḥ vetanena yathāyogyaṃ priyavādena cāpare
english: And many warriors were maintained, great car-warriors taken on only after testing, with fitting pay—and others with kindly words.

sanskrit: akāraṇabhṛtas tāta mama sainye na vidyate karmaṇā hy anurūpeṇa labhyate bhaktavetanam
english: In my army, my son, there is none kept on without cause; for the wages of a retainer are earned by service that befits them.

sanskrit: na ca yodho 'bhavat kaś cin mama sainye tu saṃjaya alpadānabhṛtas tāta na kupyabhṛtako naraḥ
english: And there was not, O Saṃjaya, a single warrior in my army maintained on scant gifts, my son, nor any man hired with paltry goods.

sanskrit: pūjitā hi yathāśaktyā dānamānāsanair mayā tathā putraiś ca me tāta jñātibhiś ca sabāndhavaiḥ
english: For they were honoured to my utmost means with gifts, with respect, and with seats of rank—by me, and by my sons, my son, and by my kinsmen and their relations alike.

sanskrit: te ca prāpyaiva saṃgrāme nirjitāḥ savyasācinā śaineyena parāmṛṣṭāḥ kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: Yet these very men, when they met them in battle, were vanquished by Savyasācin and overwhelmed by the grandson of Śini. What is this but the work of destiny?

sanskrit: rakṣyate yaś ca saṃgrāme ye ca saṃjaya rakṣiṇaḥ ekaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ panthā rakṣyasya saha rakṣibhiḥ
english: He who is guarded in battle, O Saṃjaya, and those who are his guardians—one common road lies before the guarded and his guards alike.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ samare dṛṣṭvā saindhavasyāgrataḥ sthitam putro mama bhṛśaṃ mūḍhaḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ pratyapadyata
english: Seeing Arjuna stationed in battle before the Saindhava, what course did my son, sorely bewildered, resolve upon?

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ ca raṇe dṛṣṭvā praviśantam abhītavat kiṃ nu duryodhanaḥ kṛtyaṃ prāptakālam amanyata
english: And seeing Sātyaki entering the battle fearlessly, what task fit for the hour did Duryodhana then deem to be his?

sanskrit: sarvaśastrātigau senāṃ praviṣṭau rathasattamau dṛṣṭvā kāṃ vai dhṛtiṃ yuddhe pratyapadyanta māmakāḥ
english: Seeing those two best of car-warriors, surpassing all in arms, enter the army, what firmness in the fight did my people muster?

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ tu dāśārham arjunārthe vyavasthitam śinīnām ṛṣabhaṃ caiva manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Beholding Kṛṣṇa the Dāśārha set there for Arjuna's sake, and the bull of the Śinis as well, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā senāṃ vyatikrāntāṃ sātvatenārjunena ca palāyamānāṃś ca kurūn manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Seeing the army broken through by the Sātvata and by Arjuna, and the Kurus in flight, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: vidrutān rathino dṛṣṭvā nirutsāhān dviṣajjaye palāyane kṛtotsāhān manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Seeing the car-warriors scattered, void of zeal to conquer the foe and bent all their zeal upon flight, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: śūnyān kṛtān rathopasthān sātvatenārjunena ca hatāṃś ca yodhān saṃdṛśya manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Beholding the chariot-platforms emptied by the Sātvata and by Arjuna, and the warriors slain, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: vyaśvanāgarathān dṛṣṭvā tatra vīrān sahasraśaḥ dhāvamānān raṇe vyagrān manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Seeing heroes there by the thousand, stripped of horses, elephants, and chariots, running distraught about the field, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: vivīrāṃś ca kṛtān aśvān virathāṃś ca kṛtān narān tatra sātyakipārthābhyāṃ manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Seeing the horses left riderless and the men left chariotless there by Sātyaki and Pārtha, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: pattisaṃghān raṇe dṛṣṭvā dhāvamānāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ nirāśā vijaye sarve manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Seeing the bands of foot-soldiers running every which way in the battle, all of them despairing of victory, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: droṇasya samatikrāntāv anīkam aparājitau kṣaṇena dṛṣṭvā tau vīrau manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Seeing those two unconquered heroes break clean through Droṇa's division in an instant, I think my poor sons are grieving.

sanskrit: saṃmūḍho 'smi bhṛśaṃ tāta śrutvā kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau praviṣṭau māmakaṃ sainyaṃ sātvatena sahācyutau
english: I am sorely bewildered, my son, to hear that Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya, together with the Sātvata, those unfaltering ones, have entered my army.

sanskrit: tasmin praviṣṭe pṛtanāṃ śinīnāṃ pravare rathe bhojānīkaṃ vyatikrānte katham āsan hi kauravāḥ
english: When that foremost car-warrior of the Śinis had entered the host and broken through the Bhoja division, how then fared the Kauravas?

sanskrit: tathā droṇena samare nigṛhīteṣu pāṇḍuṣu kathaṃ yuddham abhūt tatra tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: And when the Pāṇḍavas were held in check by Droṇa in the battle, how did the fighting go there? Tell me that, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: droṇo hi balavāñ śūraḥ kṛtāstro dṛḍhavikramaḥ pāñcālās taṃ maheṣvāsaṃ pratyayudhyan kathaṃ raṇe
english: For Droṇa is strong, a hero, accomplished in arms, and firm in valour; how did the Pāñcālas fight against that great archer in the battle?

sanskrit: baddhavairās tathā droṇe dharmarājajayaiṣiṇaḥ bhāradvājas tathā teṣu kṛtavairo mahārathaḥ
english: They had sworn a bitter feud with Droṇa and sought the Dharma-king's victory; and the great car-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja, had likewise sworn enmity against them.

sanskrit: arjunaś cāpi yac cakre sindhurājavadhaṃ prati tan me sarvaṃ samācakṣva kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: And whatever Arjuna did toward the slaying of the king of the Sindhus, tell me all of that, O Saṃjaya, for you are skilled in the telling.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ātmāparādhāt saṃbhūtaṃ vyasanaṃ bharatarṣabha prāpya prākṛtavad vīra na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: Saṃjaya said: This calamity has arisen from your own offence, O bull of the Bharatas; having met with it, O hero, you ought not to grieve like a common man.

sanskrit: tava nirguṇatāṃ jñātvā pakṣapātaṃ suteṣu ca dvaidhībhāvaṃ tathā dharme pāṇḍaveṣu ca matsaram ārtapralāpāṃś ca bahūn manujādhipasattama
english: Knowing your want of virtue, your partiality toward your sons, your double-mindedness in matters of duty, your spite against the Pāṇḍavas, and your many wails of distress, O best of rulers of men—

sanskrit: sarvalokasya tattvajñaḥ sarvalokaguruḥ prabhuḥ vāsudevas tato yuddhaṃ kurūṇām akaron mahat
english: Vāsudeva, the lord who knows the truth of all the worlds, the teacher of all the worlds, thereupon brought about this great war of the Kurus.

sanskrit: ātmāparādhāt sumahān prāptas te vipulaḥ kṣayaḥ na hi te sukṛtaṃ kiṃ cid ādau madhye ca bhārata dṛśyate pṛṣṭhataś caiva tvanmūlo hi parājayaḥ
english: From your own offence has this exceedingly vast destruction come upon you; for no good deed of yours is seen at the beginning, nor in the middle, nor at the end, O Bhārata—the defeat has its root in you alone.
